body:
## Summary

When uv scans the search path for an interpreter, a `python` on `PATH` that **fails to execute** (non-zero exit) aborts the entire discovery with a hard error, instead of being skipped like any other unusable candidate. One broken executable early on `PATH` makes uv unusable on a machine that has half a dozen working interpreters.

The error message itself says *"first executable in the search path"* — uv knows this is one candidate among many, and still treats its failure as fatal.

## Why this is easy to hit: pyenv always installs a `python` shim

pyenv creates a `~/.pyenv/shims/python` shim unconditionally. But the shim only *works* if the currently selected version actually provides a `python` binary. With `pyenv global system` on a macOS box whose system Python is Homebrew's `python@3.14` (which ships `python3` but no `python`), the shim exits 127:

```console
$ ~/.pyenv/shims/python --version
pyenv: python: command not found

The `python' command exists in these Python versions:
  3.11.10
  3.12.3
$ echo $?
127
```

That is a completely ordinary pyenv setup — nothing misconfigured, `python3` works fine — and it takes uv down.

## Reproduction (no pyenv needed)

```console
$ mkdir -p /tmp/fakeshim
$ cat > /tmp/fakeshim/python <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
echo "pyenv: python: command not found" >&2
exit 127
EOF
$ chmod +x /tmp/fakeshim/python
$ export PATH="/tmp/fakeshim:$PATH"

$ echo 'print("hello")' > /tmp/t.py
$ UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never uv run --no-project --python 3.13 /tmp/t.py
error: Failed to inspect Python interpreter from first executable in the search path at `/tmp/fakeshim/python`
  Caused by: Querying Python at `/tmp/fakeshim/python` failed with exit status exit status: 127

    [stderr]
    pyenv: python: command not found
```

A working 3.13 elsewhere on `PATH` is never reached, because the scan stops at the broken candidate.

Note the failure only shows up when uv has to scan — a request satisfiable from the first working match, or from a managed/downloaded interpreter, hides it:

```console
$ uv run --no-project /tmp/t.py     # same broken PATH
hello
```

That makes it confusing in practice: uv appears to work, then fails on the one project that pins a version needing a real search.

## Expected behaviour

A candidate that cannot be queried is not a valid interpreter — skip it and continue the scan, ideally with a warning (or a `-v` trace line). Aborting is only appropriate if the failing executable was *explicitly requested* (e.g. `--python /path/to/it`).

## Actual behaviour

Discovery aborts with a hard error and a non-zero exit.

## Real-world impact

Hit while running a project-pinned tool via `uv run --project …`. On this machine every uv invocation that needed a scan failed, and the message points at the pyenv shim rather than at anything the user asked for — the fix (`pyenv global system 3.12.3`, so the shim resolves) is not discoverable from the error. Downgrading isn't relevant; this reproduces on the current release.

## Environment

- uv 0.12.3 (Homebrew 2026-08-07 aarch64-apple-darwin)
- macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0), arm64
- pyenv with `global system` and Homebrew `python@3.14` as the system Python

## Possibly related, but not duplicates

- #4958 (closed) — uv not searching past a default interpreter of the *wrong version*. Here the candidate does not run at all.
- #13402, #2109, #12155 — other pyenv interactions, none about a non-zero-exit candidate aborting the scan.
title: Interpreter discovery aborts on a PATH candidate that fails to execute (pyenv shim, exit 127) instead of skipping it
